text:
I’ll never forget the day I ordered a Dr Pepper at McDonald’s, expecting the usual burst of that unique blend of 23 flavors. Instead, what I received was a watery, diluted mess. The first sip hit me like a wave of disappointment, a shadow of what Dr Pepper is supposed to be. It felt like a betrayal, as if all the joy and energy I was counting on to get through the rest of my day had been drained away along with the syrup. What was supposed to be a quick pick-me-up turned into the start of a downward spiral.

From that moment, everything seemed to go wrong. My productivity plummeted, my mood soured, and my ability to focus on work slipped away with every diluted sip. The frustration lingered long after the taste faded. I began questioning my decisions, starting with the small ones like trusting McDonald’s to deliver a decent soft drink, then slowly spiraling into deeper thoughts about my life choices. Something as simple as a poorly mixed Dr Pepper shouldn’t have had that much power over me, yet here I was, feeling as though my life had been derailed by a disappointing beverage.

In the weeks that followed, I found myself avoiding fast food restaurants altogether, fearing another run-in with a watery soda. It became a symbol of everything that had gone wrong—small disappointments building into larger issues. Relationships seemed to strain, deadlines became more overwhelming, and even the smallest of inconveniences felt magnified. That one watered-down Dr Pepper had planted a seed of dissatisfaction that grew and festered, leaving me with a bitter reminder of how even the smallest things can throw life completely off balance.
author: jack

text: I recently visited the 526 ponce de leon ave mcdonald's location on 12/6/22 at 3:28 AM. I placed a mobile order and proceeded to the speaker to give my code. When I got there, I said "Hello!" and heard a very loud yell "HOLD UP."  I told her "Why are you yelling at me?" and she said "why are you saying Hello?" I then told her (very appalled that this was why this woman was yelling), "to let you know that I'm at the window." I then gave her my order number and when I approached the 1st window, I asked what her name was. She then looked at me straight in the face and closed the window and walked away to the 2nd window. At the second window she told me "Quisha, my name is Quisha!" and just stood there. I asked her if she had taken my order and she confirmed she did. There were 3 other workers around her. I then told her "That's all I need to know." She then responded "Oh, I know." I then asked to speak to a manager and with all the 4 staff there, the same woman who yelled at me at the speaker, said she was the manager. I was in disbelief. I live 3 minutes away and always come to this McDonalds and had never been treated so poorly by staff here. I truly hope that this message reaches a management that actually cares about their customers because the "management" I supposedly encountered, clearly did not. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone I know given what I experienced here on behalf of "management." NOTE: the receipt says "SIDEL" took my order.  Please let me know if there is any more information, I can provide you. Also, find attached the receipt of purchase.

text:
I’ve been a loyal customer at this location for over 30 years, coming in almost daily. Most of the staff, including James and Lupita, are always polite and professional. Unfortunately, one manager, Cora, is consistently rude and makes my visits unpleasant.

Every time she’s working, she goes out of her way to harass me. Most recently, I ordered a drink through the drive-thru, parked, went inside to buy food, and refilled my soda while waiting. She refused to hand me my bag, stared at my cup, and then told me drive-thru customers aren’t allowed refills. In 30 years of visiting, I’ve never heard of that rule.

This isn’t the first problem. She once personally asked me for $40, which I gave her out of kindness, and ever since then she’s treated me with hostility. I’ve even filed several complaints (at least four over the last two years). After each one she pretends to be pleasant for a short time, then goes right back to the same behavior.

It’s gotten to the point where I avoid the store if I see her car outside. No customer should feel that unwelcome, especially someone who has supported this location for decades. Corporate really needs to step in and address this manager before more loyal customers are driven away.
author: Lloyd Thurston Dinwiddie AkA Gyant

text:
visited this McDonald’s on 11/5 with my daughter, who wanted the 2-sandwich meal. When we pulled off and opened the bag, one of the sandwiches was just bread — no meat at all. I had to turn all the way back around to get it corrected, which was already inconvenient since we live in Acworth.

When we arrived, I politely explained what happened and simply asked if we could get two cookies for the inconvenience. The young lady at the first window was kind and apologetic, and she said that would be fine. However, when we got to the second window, an employee named James told me he didn’t believe there was “only bread” in the wrapper and that my kids had probably dropped the sandwich.

That comment was completely uncalled for. To accuse me — and especially my children — of lying over a missing sandwich was disrespectful and unnecessary. I would have been honest if that were the case, but it wasn’t. His attitude and assumptions made me feel completely disrespected.

This kind of behavior is unacceptable, and it shows a serious lack of customer service and professionalism. It’s especially disappointing because it felt like we were being judged simply because I’m a Black mother with children. Do better, McDonald’s.
author: Sky Rose Channel

text:
I almost never write bad reviews. However this was by far one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had. Mind you, I’ve worked in restaurants for over 5 years to include fast food.

We waited over 15 minutes in the drive through, only for them to tell us to come inside. After placing our order and waiting another 20+ minutes, did we receive our order.

While we waited, the whole staff was lost tracking all the orders coming through. The cashier straight up did not have a care in the world, and one employee even just straight up walked out.

To top it off, they even got our entire order wrong even after we had told them what we got. We were missing items and my order was wrong too. We were sick and tired of waiting and just decided to take it and go.

This was a complete and utter failure, if I could rate it lower, I would. This experience shouldn’t be allowed to exist and I pity those who came through that night. Heed my words; never come through this restaraunt during a rush.
